text.p: Connective Therapeutics Inc said Phase II trials of gamma interferon in patients with severe atopic dermatitis produced a statistically significant improvement.
The company said the amount of skin area affected by the disease at the start of the trials averaged 62 percent, and was cut to an average 19 percent after the gamma interferon therapy.

"These results are particularly encouraging as we near completion of our Phase III clinical trial of gamma interferon in severe atopic dermatitis," W. Scott Harkonen, senior vice president of product development at Connective said in a statement.

"It is our goal to report data from the Phase III trial by year end and, with positive results, plan to submit an application with the FDA to begin marketing gamma interferon in the U.S. for the treatment of atopic dermatitis."
